question.text: Under the Income Tax Act (Section 80C treatment), what is the compulsory lock-in period for ELSS (Equity Linked Savings Scheme) investments?

answer.text: 5 years from the date of investment
3 years from the date of investment
1 year from the date of investment
3 years from the end of the financial year of investment

explanation.text: The Logic: ELSS has a compulsory lock-in period of 3 years from the date of investment. This is the shortest lock-in among Section 80C qualifying instruments. For SIP investments in ELSS, each instalment is locked in for 3 years from its own date of investment. The Trap: Option A (5 years) applies to tax-saving bank FDs and NSC, not ELSS. Option C (1 year) is too short. Option D wrongly counts from the end of the financial year - the lock-in runs from the date of investment. Note: Sources - NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (November 2025), p. 161, which states the ELSS lock-in runs from the date of investment; and NISM Series X-B Investment Adviser (Level 2) workbook, p. 240, which confirms the compulsory 3-year ELSS lock-in.
